methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $165M total raised proxy.

private.name: Meter
private.rationale: Same sector (Housing & Construction), same stage (Series C)

data.narrative:
ICON is a Series C-stage housing and construction company that has raised $450M+ to date. The comp universe for this stage and sector is sparse, comprising one identified private peer (Meter) and no public comparables, limiting the strength of cross-sectional benchmarking.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation framework given data constraints. Using total capital raised ($450M+) as a proxy anchor, the analysis imputes a base value of $165M. Applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $280M. This represents the median point of the triangulated range.

The valuation analysis supports a range of $238M to $323M, with a central estimate of $280M. This range incorporates a ±15% variance around the median to reflect both upside and downside scenario uncertainty. Key limitations include reliance on a single valuation method, insufficient public or private comparables for cross-validation, and the absence of ICON's disclosed financials. The stage-progression approach is most sensitive to assumptions about typical multiplier step-ups between Series C and later funding rounds in construction technology. Additional data on revenue, growth rates, and performance of private peers would materially improve confidence in this range.
